profile.bio: I am a Professor of Nutrition and Internal Medicine at the University of California Davis. My research program investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying metabolic homeostasis, including type 2 diabetes (T2D) and its complications. We employ genetic, pharmacological, biochemical, and metabolomics approaches to decipher the role of protein tyrosine phosphatases (PTPs) in metabolic regulation. works.abstract: Objectives: Microplastics (MP) and nanoplastics (NP) are a growing health concern globally. Microplastics (MP) have emerged as environmental pollutant due to the risks they pose to both wildlife and human health. The breakdown of plastics leads to the formation of high amounts of MPs and NPs. This has led to animal consumption within their natural environments, accumulating up the food chain. MPs and NPs can further be consumed through contamination during food production and leaching from packaging surrounding food and drinks.
works.title: Adverse Effects of Nanoplastics Administration on the Metabolic Profile and Glucose Control in Mice

works.abstract: Objectives: Nanoplastics (NP) are a growing global health concern posing risks to both wildlife and human health. Polystyrene plastics, commonly used in food packaging, can break down into smaller micro- and nanoplastics. These NP can contaminate food and beverages during production, processing, and from leaching of packaging. Further, NP have emerged as an environmental pollutant leading to animal consumption within their natural environments, and bioaccumulation up the food chain. While human exposure to NP continues through food, products, water, and air, the toxicity and implications for health have yet to be fully understood.
works.title: Polystyrene Nanoplastic Administration Alters Metabolic and Lipid Profiles in Peripheral Insulin-Sensitive Tissues
